{{Short description|American chemist (1927–2026)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=June 2020}}
{{Use American English|date=February 2026}}
'''Kenneth Berle Wiberg''' (September 22, 1927 – May 10, 2026) was an American chemist and academic who was Professor Emeritus of [[organic chemistry]] at [[Yale University]]. He contributed to many aspects of organic chemistry including physical and synthetic aspects.<ref>{{cite book|title=Laboratory Technique in Organic Chemistry|author=Kenneth B. Wiberg|isbn=0070700958|year=1960|publisher=McGraw-Hill}}</ref><ref name="MPC-object" />

==Scholarship==
In the area of synthetic organic chemistry, Wiberg and his students reported the preparation of highly strained organic compounds [[bicyclobutane]]<ref>{{cite journal|first1 = K. B.|last1 = Wiberg|first2 = G. M.|last2 = Lampman|first3 = R. P.|last3 = Ciula|first4 = D. S.|last4 = Connor|first5 = P.|last5 = Schertler|first6 = J.|last6 = Lavanish|title = Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane|journal = [[Tetrahedron (journal)|Tetrahedron]]|year = 1965|volume = 21|issue = 10|pages = 2749–2769|doi = 10.1016/S0040-4020(01)98361-9}}</ref> and [[1.1.1-Propellane|[1.1.1]propellane]]:<ref>{{cite journal|first1=K. B.|last1=Wiberg|first2=F. H.|last2=Walker|date=1982|title=[1.1.1]Propellane|journal=[[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]]|volume=104|issue=19|pages=5239–5240|doi=10.1021/ja00383a046|bibcode=1982JAChS.104.5239W }}</ref>

:[[File:111propellaneSynthesis.png|thumb|none|400px|'''Scheme 1.''' Synthesis of [1.1.1]propellane]]

==Death==
Wiberg died in [[Needham, Massachusetts]], on May 10, 2026, at the age of 98.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kenneth B. Wiberg |url=https://www.tributearchive.com/obituaries/48393243/kenneth-b.-wiberg |website=Tribute Archive |access-date=18 May 2026}}</ref>

==Recognition==
* Wiberg was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and an [[American Association of Arts and Sciences]] fellow.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://ursula.chem.yale.edu/faculty/wiberg.html |title= Kenneth B. Wiberg, Faculty |publisher= [[Yale University]] Department of Chemistry |access-date= March 15, 2017 |archive-date= May 2, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170502120934/http://ursula.chem.yale.edu/faculty/wiberg.html |url-status= dead }}</ref>
* In 1988, he won the [[Arthur C. Cope Award]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/arthur-c-cope-award.html |title= Arthur C. Cope Award |publisher= [[American Chemical Society]] }}</ref>
* Asteroid [[27267 Wiberg]], discovered by American astronomer [[John V. McClusky]] at Fair Oaks Ranch Observatory {{Obscode|725}} in 1999, was named in his honor.<ref name="MPC-object" /> The official {{MoMP|27267|naming citation}} was published by the [[Minor Planet Center]] on 7 January 2004 ({{small|[[Minor Planet Circulars|M.P.C.]] 50464}}).<ref name="MPC-Circulars-Archive" />
